description: Pineapple Buns, or Bo Lo Bao, are a beloved classic from Hong Kong bakeries, famous for their unique crispy, sweet crust resembling a pineapple's skin, though they contain no actual pineapple. Beneath this irresistible topping lies a soft, fluffy, slightly sweet bread, making them a perfect treat for breakfast or a snack. This recipe guides you to recreate that authentic bakery experience right in your own kitchen.

cold, cubed, for the pineapple topping

instructions.title: Prepare the Bread Dough
instructions.text: In a large bowl, combine 250g all-purpose flour, 30g granulated sugar, 4g instant dry yeast, and 3g salt. Add 120ml lukewarm milk and most of the beaten egg (reserve 1 tbsp for egg wash). Mix until a shaggy dough forms. Turn onto a lightly floured surface and knead for 8-10 minutes until smooth and elastic. Incorporate the 25g softened unsalted butter and knead for another 5 minutes until fully absorbed and the dough is smooth and pliable.

instructions.title: First Proofing
instructions.text: Place the kneaded bread dough in a lightly oiled bowl, turning once to coat. Cover the bowl tightly with plastic wrap or a damp cloth. Let it rise in a warm, draft-free place for 60-90 minutes, or until the dough has visibly doubled in size.

instructions.title: Make the Pineapple Topping
instructions.text: While the bread dough is proofing, prepare the topping. In a separate bowl, combine 120g all-purpose flour, 80g granulated sugar, 1 tbsp powdered milk, and 1/2 tsp baking powder. Add the 60g cold, cubed unsalted butter and cut it into the dry ingredients using a pastry blender or your fingertips until the mixture resembles coarse crumbs. Stir in the 1 large egg yolk and 1 tbsp evaporated milk until a soft dough forms. Do not overmix. Wrap the topping dough in plastic wrap and chill it in the refrigerator for at least 30 minutes.

instructions.title: Shape the Buns
instructions.text: Once the bread dough has completed its first proofing, gently punch it down to release the air. Transfer the dough to a lightly floured surface and divide it into 8 equal portions. Roll each portion into a smooth, round ball. Place these shaped bread balls onto a parchment-lined baking sheet, ensuring there is sufficient space between each bun for expansion.

instructions.title: Apply the Topping
instructions.text: Retrieve the chilled pineapple topping dough from the refrigerator. Divide it into 8 equal portions. On a lightly floured surface or between two sheets of parchment paper, flatten each portion of topping dough into a thin disc, approximately 3-4 inches in diameter. Carefully drape each topping disc over a bread dough ball, gently pressing down to adhere it, covering about two-thirds of the bun. Use a knife to lightly score a crisscross pattern on the surface of the pineapple topping.

instructions.title: Second Proofing and Bake
instructions.text: Cover the shaped buns loosely with plastic wrap or a light cloth and let them rise in a warm place for another 30-45 minutes, or until visibly puffy. While they rise, preheat your oven to 180°C (350°F). Whisk the reserved 1 tbsp beaten egg with 1 tsp water to create an egg wash. Lightly brush the pineapple topping (avoiding the exposed bread dough) with this egg wash. Bake for 18-22 minutes, or until the topping is golden brown and crispy, and the buns are cooked through.

instructions.title: Cool and Serve
instructions.text: Remove the freshly baked Pineapple Buns from the oven. Carefully transfer them to a wire rack to cool slightly. Pineapple Buns are best enjoyed warm, allowing the crispy topping and soft interior to be fully appreciated. Serve them plain or with a slice of butter tucked inside for an authentic Hong Kong cafe experience.

tips: To achieve the perfect crispy topping, ensure your butter for the topping is very cold. Work quickly to prevent it from melting too much, which can make the topping greasy instead of crumbly.
For an extra fluffy bread interior, use bread flour instead of all-purpose flour for the dough. This adds more gluten, resulting in a chewier texture.
Pineapple Buns are best enjoyed fresh on the day they are baked. If you have leftovers, reheat them gently in a toaster oven for a few minutes to crisp up the topping again.
article:
The aroma of freshly baked bread, sweet and buttery, is a universal comfort. In the vibrant world of Chinese baking, few treats are as iconic and beloved as Bo Lo Bao, or the Pineapple Bun. With its distinctive golden, crumbly topping and cloud-soft interior, this pastry has captured hearts from Hong Kong tea houses to bakeries across the globe. Despite its name, you won't find a single piece of pineapple within its delightful layers. Instead, the "pineapple" refers to the signature crisscross pattern on its crispy crust, which beautifully resembles the fruit's rough skin. If you've ever dreamt of recreating this bakery masterpiece in your own kitchen, you're in the right place. This article will guide you through the magic of Bo Lo Bao, demystifying its creation and empowering you to bake your very own batch of these irresistible buns.

## What is a Pineapple Bun (Bo Lo Bao)?

At its heart, a Pineapple Bun is a marvel of contrasts. It starts with an enriched, milky bread dough, similar to a brioche, that bakes up incredibly soft, fluffy, and slightly sweet. This tender base is then crowned with a unique, cookie-like topping, made from flour, sugar, butter, and egg. When baked, this topping expands and cracks, forming a delightful, slightly sandy, sweet crust that provides the "pineapple" appearance and a satisfying textural counterpoint to the airy bread beneath.

Originating in Hong Kong, Bo Lo Bao quickly became a staple in cha chaan tengs (Hong Kong-style diners) and traditional bakeries. It's often enjoyed as a breakfast item, an afternoon snack, or alongside a cup of Hong Kong-style milk tea. While the classic version is plain, allowing the interplay of the bun and crust to shine, variations with fillings like a slab of cold butter (Bo Lo Yau), custard, red bean paste, or even savory char siu (BBQ pork) have gained immense popularity. Understanding the balance of textures and flavors is key to appreciating this culinary icon.

## Ingredients for Homemade Pineapple Buns

Crafting the perfect Pineapple Bun involves two main components: the soft, enriched dough and the distinctive, crumbly topping. Gathering your ingredients before you begin will make the process smooth and enjoyable.

For the Enriched Bun Dough:
*   3 cups (360g) all-purpose flour, plus more for dusting
*   1/4 cup (50g) granulated sugar
*   1 teaspoon instant yeast
*   1/2 teaspoon salt
*   1 large egg, room temperature
*   1 cup (240ml) warm milk (around 105-115°F / 40-46°C)
*   1/4 cup (56g) unsalted butter, softened

For the Pineapple Topping (Bo Lo Bao Topping):
*   1/2 cup (113g) unsalted butter, softened
*   1/2 cup (100g) granulated sugar (or powdered sugar for a finer crumb)
*   1 large egg yolk
*   1 1/2 cups (180g) all-purpose flour
*   1 tablespoon milk powder (optional, for added richness and flavor)
*   1/2 teaspoon vanilla extract

For the Egg Wash:
*   1 large egg yolk
*   1 tablespoon milk or water

## Step-by-Step Guide to Making Bo Lo Bao

Making Pineapple Buns from scratch is a rewarding process that, while requiring a bit of time, is surprisingly straightforward. This comprehensive Pineapple Bun Recipe will walk you through each stage.

1.  **Prepare the Bun Dough:** In a large bowl, whisk together the flour, sugar, yeast, and salt. In a separate bowl, lightly beat the egg and warm milk. Pour the wet ingredients into the dry ingredients and mix until a shaggy dough forms. Turn the dough out onto a lightly floured surface and knead for about 10 minutes, until smooth and elastic. Gradually incorporate the softened butter, continuing to knead until the butter is fully absorbed and the dough is very smooth and pliable.
2.  **First Rise:** Place the dough in a lightly oiled bowl, cover with plastic wrap, and let it rise in a warm place for 1 to 1.5 hours, or until doubled in size.
3.  **Make the Pineapple Topping:** While the dough rises, prepare the topping. In a medium bowl, cream together the softened butter and sugar until light and fluffy. Beat in the egg yolk and vanilla extract until well combined. Gradually add the flour and milk powder (if using), mixing until just combined and a crumbly dough forms. Do not overmix. Gather the topping dough into a ball, flatten slightly, wrap in plastic, and chill in the refrigerator for at least 30 minutes.
4.  **Shape the Buns:** Once the dough has doubled, punch it down gently to release the air. Divide the dough into 8-10 equal pieces (around 70-80g each). Roll each piece into a smooth ball. Place them on a baking sheet lined with parchment paper, leaving space between each.
5.  **Apply the Topping:** Take the chilled topping dough and divide it into the same number of pieces as your buns. On a lightly floured surface or between two sheets of parchment paper, roll out each piece of topping dough into a flat, thin circle, slightly larger than the top of your bun. Carefully drape a topping circle over each bun, gently pressing to adhere it to the top.
6.  **Score the Topping:** Using a sharp knife or a dough scraper, gently score a crisscross pattern on the top of each bun. Be careful not to cut too deeply into the bread dough itself.
7.  **Second Rise:** Cover the buns loosely with plastic wrap or a clean kitchen towel and let them rise in a warm place for another 30-45 minutes, or until visibly puffy.
8.  **Egg Wash and Bake:** Preheat your oven to 375°F (190°C). In a small bowl, whisk the egg yolk and milk/water for the egg wash. Gently brush the tops of the buns (especially the topping) with the egg wash. Bake for 15-20 minutes, or until the topping is golden brown and cracked, and the buns are cooked through. This detailed Pineapple Bun Recipe guides you through each crucial stage.

## Tips for Perfect Pineapple Buns

Achieving that bakery-quality Pineapple Bun requires a few key techniques. Mastering the steps in this Pineapple Bun Recipe will elevate your baking from good to extraordinary.

*   **Don't Skimp on Kneading:** For the bun dough, thorough kneading is essential to develop the gluten, which gives the bread its signature soft and airy texture. If you have a stand mixer, use it with a dough hook for about 8-10 minutes. By hand, it might take 15-20 minutes. The dough should pass the "windowpane test" – you should be able to stretch a small piece thin enough to see light through it without tearing.
*   **Proofing Environment:** Yeast loves warmth and humidity. If your kitchen is cool, you can create a makeshift proofing box by placing the covered dough in a slightly warm (but turned off) oven with a pan of hot water on the rack below.
*   **Topping Consistency:** The topping should be firm enough to handle without being sticky, but not so dry that it cracks excessively when rolled. If it's too soft, chill it longer. If too dry, add a tiny bit of milk, half a teaspoon at a time.
*   **Gentle Handling:** When applying the topping and scoring, be gentle. You want to adhere the topping and create the pattern without deflating the risen dough.
*   **Egg Wash for Shine:** The egg wash not only gives the topping a beautiful golden sheen but also helps it crisp up nicely.
*   **Hot Oven for a Quick Rise:** Starting with a relatively hot oven helps the buns "spring" quickly, giving them a good rise and helping the topping to crack beautifully.

## Serving Suggestions & Variations

The classic Pineapple Bun is a versatile treat, delicious on its own or enhanced with various accompaniments.

*   **The Classic Bo Lo Yau:** The most iconic way to enjoy a warm Pineapple Bun is sliced horizontally and filled with a thick slab of cold, unsalted butter. The contrast between the warm, sweet bun and the cold, salty butter is pure heaven.
*   **Savory Surprises:** For a more substantial meal, Pineapple Buns can be filled with savory ingredients. The most popular is a sweet and savory BBQ pork (char siu) filling, creating a delightful fusion of flavors.
*   **Sweet Fillings:** Beyond butter, you can experiment with sweet fillings like homemade custard cream, red bean paste, or even a dollop of fruit jam.
*   **With Your Favorite Brew:** Pineapple Buns pair perfectly with a strong cup of Hong Kong-style milk tea or coffee, making them an ideal breakfast or afternoon tea companion.
*   **Creative Toppings:** While the traditional topping is king, some variations include a sprinkle of toasted sesame seeds or shredded coconut before baking for added texture and aroma.

## Common Questions About Pineapple Buns

Many people are curious about the intricacies of this unique pastry. Here are answers to some common questions about Bo Lo Bao, helping you understand this Pineapple Bun Recipe even better.

*   **Q: Is there actual pineapple in a Pineapple Bun?**
    A: No, despite the name, there is no pineapple fruit in a Pineapple Bun. The name comes from the distinct crisscross pattern on the sweet, crumbly topping, which resembles the rough skin of a pineapple.

*   **Q: What makes the topping so crispy and unique?**
    A: The topping is essentially a simple shortbread-like cookie dough. It's made from butter, sugar, flour, and egg yolk. When baked, it cooks faster than the bread underneath, creating a crisp, crumbly crust that cracks and expands. The high fat content in the butter contributes to its tenderness and melt-in-your-mouth texture.

*   **Q: Can I make the dough or topping ahead of time?**
    A: Yes, absolutely! You can prepare the bun dough and let it have its first rise in the refrigerator overnight. This slows down the fermentation and can even enhance the flavor. The topping dough can also be made a day or two in advance and stored tightly wrapped in the refrigerator. Just bring it to a workable temperature before rolling.

*   **Q: Why did my topping slide off during baking?**
    A: This can happen if the topping is too soft (too warm) or if the surface of your bun is too smooth or oily, preventing proper adhesion. Ensure your topping is chilled and firm when you apply it, and gently press it onto the bun. A light dusting of flour on the bun before applying the topping can also help. Many people wonder if this Pineapple Bun Recipe is difficult, but with practice, it's quite manageable.

*   **Q: What if I don't have milk powder for the topping?**
    A: Milk powder is optional but recommended for an extra layer of richness and a slightly more authentic flavor. If you don't have it, you can simply omit it, and your topping will still be delicious. A common question regarding any Pineapple Bun Recipe is about ingredient substitutions, and for milk powder, it's easily skipped.

There's an undeniable satisfaction in pulling a tray of warm, fragrant Pineapple Buns from your own oven. The golden crust, the sweet aroma, and the promise of that fluffy interior are truly a baker's delight. This comprehensive guide and Pineapple Bun Recipe has hopefully inspired you to embark on this delightful baking journey. Don't be intimidated; with a little patience and these step-by-step instructions, you'll soon be enjoying your very own homemade Bo Lo Bao, a taste of Hong Kong right in your kitchen. Happy baking!
